note: After the original description in Hagen 1858, Monographie der Termiten (Linnaea Entomologica 12, pp. 130—133), a Latin diagnosis with a detailed German account. Hagen describes only the alate and the soldier and not the worker; the soldier specimens came from Borneo (collected by Ida Pfeiffer in 1852) and from Penang. The original is placed in the genus Termes (Termes carbonarius), now in Macrotermes. Fractions in the German original (such as the tarsus to tibia length ratio) are damaged in the scan and are therefore not entered.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A large species, wholly jet black with a greasy lustre. Alate head large, elliptical, flatly convex, the compound eyes large and strongly projecting, the ocelli far from the compound eyes with their lower margin sunk into the head capsule, forming a pit in front of them; pronotum semicircular, wider than the head including the compound eyes. The soldier resembles M. bellicosus in general form, 15 mm long, dark coal black above, the head in front of the antennae reddish brown, the vertex with a small, slightly raised yellow spot on the posterior margin of the antennal socket as a vestige of the compound eye but without facets.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Jet black, with a greasy lustre, hairless; mouthparts, antennae and legs pale brown; wings as if varnished, semi-transparent, pale brown, the marginal vein and the basal branches of the submedia dark brown. Head large, elliptical, gently convex; compound eyes large and strongly projecting, between the occiput and the anteclypeus; occiput semicircular; vertex slightly concave, with a projecting fontanelle in the middle. Ocelli large, at a distinct distance from the compound eyes, their lower margin sunk into the head capsule so that a pit forms in front of them, the ocelli strongly directed outwards. Frons distinctly narrowing forwards, with a slight transverse impression, on both sides below the ocelli with needle-scratched fine striae. Anterior margin deeply concave, receiving the raised clypeus. Antennae as long as the head plus the pronotum, slender, 19-segmented; the basal 3 segments cylindrical, segment 1 thicker and slightly longer than wide, segment 2 shorter, segment 3 longer than segment 1 and the longest segment of the whole antenna; the remaining segments short and inverted-conical, the last oval. Labrum large, longer than wide, almost reaching the end of the mandibles, the front rounded; base strongly depressed, the distal half shell-like and raised, with a transverse impression on each side. Maxillary palps distinctly projecting beyond the mouthparts. Submentum raised into a tubercle near the labrum. Pronotum wider than the head including the compound eyes, flat, semicircular, short, more than 2 times as wide as long; anterior margin concave and upturned saddle-wise and thickened, with a shallow notch in the middle; anterior corners rounded, the sides and posterior margin forming one continuous curve; posterior margin almost not concave in the middle; anterior corners hollow, the anterior margin with a transverse impression on each side and the posterior margin with one depressed point in the middle. Meso- and metathorax large, the posterior corners rounded. Body stout, oval, flat above; the ventrolateral abdominal processes stout, conical, 4-segmented; the male styles very small, consisting of two short, separate lobes. The female has the sixth sternite large and rounded, its sides obliquely concave. Legs long, distinctly projecting beyond the body; apex of the tibia with 2 short spurs; tarsus half as long as the tibia, the last segment curved and slightly longer than the preceding segments together. Wings 4 times as long as wide; the basal third very narrow, the second third slowly widening, the apex widest, of even width and bluntly rounded; the costa strongly curved at the apex; wing scale small, truncate, rounded on the outer side; subcosta running parallel and close to the costa, merging with it a short distance before the apex; the marginal area with 1 very short branch running obliquely from the edge of the wing scale towards the costa; a short distance before the apex the subcosta gives off downwards 2—3 fine, irregular and sometimes forked branches supplying the wing apex. Media separate from the costa, first running straight, from the middle giving off 2—3 long, curved forked branches that supply the apical third of the posterior margin and anastomose with the submedia; in the hind wing the media arises from the subcosta a short distance behind the wing scale. Submedia at the middle of the wing at the same distance from the media as the media from the costa, giving off 7—8 much-curved forked branches towards the posterior margin, the first few short, straight and very strong. The whole wing membrane with irregular fine veins, especially between the subcosta and the media. Measurements: length including the wings 29 mm, body length 14 mm, wing expanse 56 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: General form as in M. bellicosus, large, 15 mm long. Above dark coal black, the underside, the end of the abdomen and the head in front of the antennae reddish brown, the underside of the head slightly darker; antennae brown with pale rings; legs yellow. Head large, flat, quadrangular, slightly longer than wide, slightly narrowing forwards, the corners rounded; anterior margin narrowed and rounded; fontanelle almost indistinguishable, with two depressed points in front of it; the sides of the head rounded below. Antennae 17-segmented, of the same shape as in the alate but with longer segments, segment 3 also the longest. Posterior margin of the antennal socket with a distinct but small, slightly raised yellow spot as a vestige of the compound eye; without facets, the cuticle there instead slightly wrinkled. Labrum large, oval, pointed. Mandibles half as long as the head, sabre-shaped, narrow, the inner margin smooth, pointed, curved inwards and upwards. Thorax large, slightly narrower than the head, slightly concave, otherwise as in M. bellicosus. Legs long and slender. Body as in M. bellicosus, the styles two short, membranous, closely approximated lobes. Body hairs sparse. A smaller soldier only 10 mm long is exactly the same colour.
